Male peepers called less often at the Brenlow ponds than at the Calder ponds.
correct_answer: Male peepers called less often at the Calder ponds than at the Ellery ponds.
explanation: Bellweather says traffic noise discourages calling "because the din drowns out their calls," while Cardenas "suspects road salt instead." Bellweather's hypothesis therefore predicts less calling at the noisy Ellery ponds than at the quiet Calder ponds, while Cardenas's account predicts less calling at the salted Calder ponds. The finding that "Male peepers called less often at the Calder ponds than at the Ellery ponds" is the opposite of what Bellweather's hypothesis predicts and fits Cardenas's, so it most directly weakens her hypothesis. The finding that "Male peepers called less often at the Ellery ponds than at the Ashby ponds" compares a noisy pond group that gets no runoff with ponds that "lie far from any road," so only noise differs and the finding supports Bellweather. The finding that "Male peepers called less often at the Brenlow ponds than at the Calder ponds" compares two groups that collect the same runoff, one noisy and one quiet, so it also supports Bellweather. The finding that "Male peepers called less often at the Brenlow ponds than at the Ashby ponds" is predicted by both accounts, since the Brenlow ponds "sit beside a highway and collect its salty runoff" and so have both noise and salt, so it cannot weaken Bellweather's hypothesis.

There were more rockfalls from the south-facing cliff in January than from the south-facing cliff in July.
correct_answer: There were more rockfalls from the north-facing cliff in July than from the north-facing cliff in March.
explanation: Grieg attributes the rockfalls to freeze-thaw cycles, while Lund attributes them to heavy rain, which falls "from June through August, when temperatures stay well above freezing." The north-facing cliff "begins to thaw by day and refreeze by night only in March and April," so on that cliff March brings freeze-thaw cycles but no heavy rain, and July brings heavy rain but no freeze-thaw cycles. The finding "There were more rockfalls from the south-facing cliff in January than from the south-facing cliff in July." supports Grieg as well, since January brings freeze-thaw cycles to the south-facing cliff while July brings it heavy rain without them.
